actor: Enforcement counsel, communications regulator's equipment authorisation programme
job: Assembling per-grant evidentiary records against Chinese humanoid, quadruped and inverter authorisations already issued, to support revoking specific grants.
outcome: A revocation order naming at least one already-authorised Chinese robot or inverter model, the instrument the prediction requires.
motivation: The commission reserved revocation power on July 28; using it is the cheapest way to close its own prospective-only gap.

task.who: Enforcement bureau equipment-authorisation staff and national-security counsel
task.what: Build revocation records against named already-authorised grants
task.where: Equipment authorisation grant files and enforcement docket
task.why: Revocation needs a per-grant record before any order issues
task.how: Equipment authorisation system records and covered-list cross-checks

actor: Rulemaking engineer, communications regulator's engineering and technology office
job: Drafting the follow-on item that would subject already-cleared Chinese robot and inverter models to the same authorisation bar.
outcome: A further notice or order whose text reaches the already-authorised population, not only models seeking new authorisation.
motivation: A rule written against unreleased models cannot answer the Volt Typhoon precedent, which is about gear already bought and installed.

task.who: Office of engineering and technology rule-drafting team
task.what: Draft retroactive-reach language for a follow-on item
task.where: Internal rulemaking drafts and commission circulation
task.why: The stated security rationale does not respect a prospective-only line
task.how: Further notice of proposed rulemaking under existing authorisation authority

actor: Professional staff, congressional select committee on strategic competition with China
job: Pressing the commission in letters, hearings and draft legislation to extend the July 28 bar to already-authorised models.
outcome: A public record of congressional demand that makes a retroactive commission step the expected next move rather than an escalation.
motivation: The committee's chair welcomed the action as strengthening domestic robotics; a carve-out leaving Chinese units on sale undercuts that claim.

task.who: Select-committee professional staff and member offices
task.what: Draft oversight letters and bill text on existing authorisations
task.where: Committee correspondence, hearing records and introduced legislation
task.why: Congressional demand converts a reserved power into an expected step
task.how: Oversight letters, hearing testimony and secure-equipment bill amendments

actor: Sanctions policy officer, treasury department China and technology desk
job: Developing designation packages against Chinese AI, robotics and inverter firms on the intellectual-property-theft grounds the treasury secretary flagged.
outcome: A designation reaching firms whose equipment is already sold, giving the commission a listed-entity hook for revoking existing grants.
motivation: Sanctions bite on the installed base a forward-only authorisation bar leaves untouched, and the secretary has already warned of them.

task.who: Treasury sanctions policy and interagency review staff
task.what: Assemble designation packages on intellectual-property-theft grounds
task.where: Interagency sanctions review and evidentiary case files
task.why: A designation reaches units already sold and installed
task.how: Intellectual-property-theft evidence and interagency designation review

actor: Manufacturing and field-operations lead, US humanoid robot maker
job: Standing up the Fremont physical-AI facility and hiring roughly 200 technical and field-operations staff to deliver Digit v5 orders.
outcome: A domestic humanoid shipping at volume, so a retroactive bar strands buyers into a substitute rather than into nothing.
motivation: More than 300 million dollars of multi-year orders convert to revenue only if the contractual milestone deliveries actually happen.

task.who: Plant engineering, production and field-deployment teams
task.what: Bring the Fremont facility to milestone delivery capacity
task.why: A funded substitute makes stranding the installed base affordable
task.how: Roughly 200 added technical and field-operations hires

actor: Capital-markets lead, special-purpose acquisition sponsor funding a domestic robot maker
job: Closing the definitive business combination at 2.5 billion dollars pre-money and releasing more than 620 million dollars of gross proceeds.
outcome: A funded, publicly listed domestic humanoid maker: the substitute whose existence lowers the political cost of reaching backwards.
motivation: The combination is expected to close during 2026, and the proceeds are what pay for the Fremont build-out and hiring.

task.who: Sponsor capital-markets team, target finance leadership and counsel
task.what: Close the business combination and release trust proceeds
task.where: Registration statement, shareholder vote and closing mechanics
task.why: Proceeds fund the domestic substitute the retroactive step assumes
task.how: Special-purpose acquisition closing with sponsor and investor commitments

actor: Grid asset-security lead, US electric utility and solar operator
job: Inventorying already-installed Chinese inverters across owned generation and distribution assets and costing a phased replacement of affected units.
outcome: A known and priced installed base of already-authorised inverters, which is what makes a retroactive bar operable rather than merely disruptive.
motivation: Remote commandeering of grid-connected inverters is the exact harm the commission cites, and the operator carries that exposure.

task.who: Asset management, procurement and operational-technology security teams
task.what: Inventory and cost replacement of installed Chinese inverters
task.where: Utility asset registers and operational-technology network inventories
task.why: A retroactive bar needs a known and replaceable installed base
task.how: Asset register audits and vendor-of-origin supply-chain review
